Oh, my goodness, yes. It's not just the physical feeling at all. Honestly, my mind just keeps going from one concern to another, almost like a... well, like a hamster wheel that someone forgot to lock. It just spins and spins. 

I mean, like I mentioned my sister earlier—she actually lives down in Arecibo, and being so far away from her right now while she's dealing with her health is just... it's a lot. I'll start worrying about her, wondering if she's telling me the whole truth about what her doctors are saying, and then before I even finish that thought, my brain just jumps right over to the office. I'll start agonizing over whether I missed something at work, you know, some little detail in the system or an email I forgot to flag that's going to cause a huge issue for the whole department. 

And then, if I manage to talk myself down from that, it's my husband. If he's even ten minutes late driving home from work, I'm immediately picturing him in some horrible accident on the interstate. I'll just be sitting there, looking out the front window, completely convinced the worst has happened. And it doesn't even stop there! It bleeds into everything—my church commitments, worrying if I dropped the ball on organizing the volunteer schedule, or the bills... even though we're doing fine financially, I just obsess over them and what would happen if some massive unexpected expense came up. 

It's just this endless loop. I find myself constantly, constantly preparing for problems that haven’t even happened yet. It's like I have to have a contingency plan for every single disaster my brain can invent, and I just can't seem to turn it off and live in the actual moment.

But in the moment, they feel just as real and just as urgent as if they were happening right in front of me. I'm not the type to just stay in bed and pull the covers over my head, even when I really, really want to. I was raised to push through, you know? You just put your head down and do what needs to be done. \n\nBut... it's definitely getting harder. It's like wading through molasses sometimes. Well, like I was just touching on a moment ago with my husband and those younger techs... yes, it really is, and it honestly breaks my heart a little bit. Because, like I said, I am usually such a patient person. I really pride myself on that. I've always been the peacekeeper in the family, the one who takes a deep breath and handles things calmly, no matter what's going on. 

But lately? My goodness, the littlest things just set me off, and I end up answering so much sharper than I mean to. It’s like my fuse is just completely gone. For example, at work, we have these documentation meetings. They're routine, we have them all the time, and usually, they're fine. But the other day, one of the team members came in with a late update to the system logs. Just a normal, run-of-the-mill delay, really nothing that was going to ruin the project. But I felt this absolute spike of irritation, and I just snapped at him in front of everyone. I was so curt. 

And it’s not just at the office where the stress is high, it’s happening in my personal life, too, even in places that are supposed to be relaxing! Like at church. I sing in the choir, and I've done that for years, I absolutely love it. But during practice recently, someone in the alto section was singing just a little bit off-tempo. Normally, I wouldn't care, I'd just smile and adjust, maybe gently help guide the section back on beat. But this time, I could feel my jaw clenching, and I actually turned and gave them this awful, sharp correction. I had to apologize profusely afterward because it was just so uncharacteristic of me. 

And then, of course, it spills over into the weekends with my family. Sundays are usually our big family dinner day, and I love cooking for everyone. I'll spend all afternoon in the kitchen. But this past Sunday, I was at the stove, just trying to get dinner finished up, and people kept coming in and out asking questions. "Where are the good napkins? Do you need me to stir that? What time exactly are we sitting down?" Just normal, harmless family chatter, you know? The kind of thing I usually love. But I just... I completely lost my temper. I barked at them to get out of my kitchen and just let me think for two seconds! I felt terrible the absolute second the words left my mouth. I just feel so guilty because I know they don't deserve it, but it's like I just don't have the emotional bandwidth to be polite when my brain is already so overloaded.

Oh, constantly. It's just constant. Everyday things are exactly what I worry about the most, even when everything is perfectly fine on paper. My mind just keeps going from one concern to another, almost like... well, in my line of work, I'd say it's like a web browser with fifty tabs open and they're all refreshing at the exact same time, and you can't figure out which one is playing the music.

And then it just shifts again. If my husband is even five minutes late driving home from work, I'm immediately picturing him in some terrible accident on the interstate. I'm literally mentally preparing for the highway patrol to knock on my front door, which I know is so completely irrational! And then from there it's church commitments—did I organize the sheet music right for Sunday, did I offend someone in the choir?—or it's the bills, worrying if the auto-pay cleared the bank properly or if someone stole our credit card number... it just never stops spinning. 

It’s so exhausting because I find myself constantly preparing for problems that haven’t even happened yet. I'm always ten steps ahead, trying to fix these elaborate disasters that only exist in my head. Like the other day, I was just folding laundry, perfectly quiet house, and suddenly I’m planning out exactly how we’d handle it if the water heater burst and ruined the downstairs. It’s never leaked a single drop, but my brain just says, 'Well, what if it does today?' and off I go, planning the insurance calls and the cleanup. I just can't seem to look at a normal, quiet day without searching for the hidden catastrophe in it.

Six months? Oh, heavens, it’s been longer than that. If I really sit and think about the timeline... yes, it’s been going on for about thirteen months now. I'll review the same spreadsheet three or four times, just paralyzed by the thought that I might have missed a decimal point or a line of code, and it just eats up hours of my day. It is utterly exhausting to work that way.\n\nAnd then, because I'm so drained from playing defense against my own brain all day, I bring that tension home with me. My nerves are just so frayed that I end up snapping at him, or my sister when she calls, and I'll just sound so terribly short with the people I care about the most.
